The biggest mistake investors make is looking only at the dividend yield or the stock price. Total return is where the real math begins.

@ZicoMorris but dividends are only a slice of growth, it is not different than growth. I never understand that debate. The dividend is the company giving you some of its growth therefore reducing it. What you don't get in price appreciation you get in dividends and vice versa. Total return is the sum of the dividend paid to you + the growth. If a company doesn't pay a dividend it doesn't matter because you can manufacture it by also selling a dividend equivalent. Selling growth never depletes capital and your share counts never gets to 0, just like a dividend does. You are not losing nor wining on either side of the debate, aside from tax consideration and market exposure.

​@LordSMif the Market goes down 50% for 3-4 years during your retirement it makes a big difference.
During that time I just live off my dividends and will not sell any stock. If I don't have any dividends I have to sell some of my stock with a 50% discount.
Makes a big difference in my book.

@tonyhickq In your mind only it makes a difference because the dividends you'll get are still a selling. You accept the loss of the dividend because you didn't press the sell button. When you live off dividends, you accept the idea of consuming part of your growth, and strangely you won't accept this idea on a growth stock? Again the dividend is just growth, look at how dividends have been slashed in 2008. If there is no growth, dividends get reduced as well. You know, a 50% decline today brings you back to 2023, depending on how long you have been investing, it means selling stocks at 350% gains instead of 400%. If you sell only 4% of the value of your balance, you are pulling the equivalent of a dividend. If you already get 2% dividend, you just sell 2%.

​@LordSMnot really. Dividends get paid in a Bear market as well, some Stocks might pay out less but most still pay out.
Therefore once the Market goes up I will still have the same amount of stock as before.
The one that has no dividends sold out during the down time the doubled amount of stock to get the same amount of money as before, therefore he lost more.
As English isn't my first language it's hard to explain more, but for me it has worked quite well for the last 40 years during every 🐻 Market.
For others other strategies might work better.
For that reason all my ETFs are distributing and not thesaurierend.

@tonyhickq I didn't say they disappeared even though it is a possibility, I said they can be reduced. My goal is not to say they're useless, just that if a stock pays one it's fine, if a stock doesn't you can make it happen yourself and it boils down to the same process. You consume part of your growth whether you call it a dividend or a capital gain.
